headline: Parliament drops anonymity for politicians in Afghanistan study
deck: Former members of a confidential committee lose the option to be quoted anonymously; the researchers hope to send the study to print before Christmas.
standard: The Presidium of the Folketing, Denmark's parliament, decided unanimously on Wednesday that former members of its confidential Foreign Policy Committee cannot be quoted anonymously in a study of Denmark's military mission in Afghanistan.

In May the Presidium had made naming them depend on their consent, arguing that they had spoken expecting 30 years of confidentiality. Veterans objected, 50,000 people signed a citizens' proposal against it, and in September the four governing parties pushed to reverse it.

Peter Kragelund, director of the Danish Institute for International Studies, whose researchers are writing the study, hopes to send it to print before Christmas, with publication probably in the new year.
short: The Presidium of the Folketing, Denmark's parliament, decided on Wednesday that former members of its confidential Foreign Policy Committee cannot be quoted anonymously in a study of Denmark's military mission in Afghanistan, reversing a decision from May. The researchers hope to send it to print before Christmas.
